findings.summary: crates/server/src/github.rs:11 and crates/server/src/main.rs:20: a fixed 30-minute unauthenticated interval doesn't fit GitHub's 60-requests-an-hour limit when one read costs about 40 requests, yet the startup warning and STATUS.md say it stays within the limit.
findings.reason: GitHub counts the requests it sends; without a token interval() waits spent*3600/45 seconds after each read (retries included), and run() asks for the interval after every read. Tested in without_a_token_reads_are_spaced_by_what_they_cost.

findings.summary: crates/server/src/github.rs:256-267 with sources.rs:117-122: a per-PR failure is swallowed and prs() returns Ok, so cards lose their gate and turn pending with last_error cleared.
findings.reason: A failed checks or records read keeps the PR's value from the last read, and the errors come back in PrRead.errors; the GitHub source reports them as Read.partial, which refresh() sets as last_error (shown by the app) and counts in board_source_read_errors_total. Tested in a_failed_part_keeps_its_earlier_value_and_marks_the_source.

findings.summary: crates/server/src/github.rs:78: a failed pulls list for one repo fails the read for every repo.
findings.reason: repo_prs errors are caught per repo; that repo keeps its last read's PRs and the error is reported. Covered by the LISTS_FAIL step of the same test.

findings.summary: crates/server/src/github.rs:81: the fork check compares full_name case-sensitively.
No test checks that a GitHub source with no token reads on the unauthenticated interval.
findings.reason: without_a_token_reads_are_spaced_by_what_they_cost asserts the exact wait for the fake's 15 requests.
